gauntlet: question
The framing holds: I checked `lib/notify.ts#post` and traced `jobs/report.ts`'s inline send and `jobs/digest.ts`'s default-channel call. All three use the same `[notice]` formatting and the same two-attempt retry loop, and no loader or runtime dependency sits outside them.

Premises:
- **Supported:** `post` owns formatting and retries but hardcodes the channel, because `lib/notify.ts:2` builds the body with `channel: "general"`.
- **Supported:** `report` duplicates `post` byte for byte except for the channel, which it takes as a parameter (`jobs/report.ts:1-6`). The duplication is the debt here, not the shared helper.

When `post` gains channel support, how should existing callers like `digest` keep working?
A) An optional channel argument that defaults to `general`, so existing calls stay untouched.
B) A required channel argument, with `"general"` written explicitly at every existing call site.
C) A separate function beside `post` for channel-targeted sends, with `post` left as is.

**(2) Approaches message**

```text
gauntlet: question
No implicit dependency was recorded as missing or not checkable. The gather trace covered `lib/notify.ts` and both callers and found no extra loader or runtime dependency, so there is nothing to restate before the approaches.

The two approaches differ on one thing: whether the channel is optional or required on the shared helper, which decides how many callers change.

I recommend **A, optional channel argument on `post`**. `post(message, channel = "general")` builds its body with the given channel. `report` stops inlining its own send and calls `post(message, channel)`. `digest` and any other existing caller compile and behave as before, since the default is exactly today's hardcoded value.

Retries and formatting stay in one place, and the duplicated loop in `report` goes away.

The trade-off is that the default stays implicit. A future caller that forgets the channel silently goes to `general`. Caller blast radius is zero beyond `report` itself.
Removes: `jobs/report.ts` inline JSON body and retry loop (the inline copy of `post`)
Adds: optional `channel: string = "general"` parameter on `post` in `lib/notify.ts`; `jobs/report.ts` call site delegating to `post(message, channel)`; notify tests covering the explicit channel, the `general` default, and retry-then-throw on both paths
Pattern: follows the owning-helper pattern by widening `post` (`lib/notify.ts:1-2`) with a backward-compatible parameter instead of keeping the parallel copy in `jobs/report.ts:2-6`.

**B, required channel argument on `post`.** This drops the assumption that a default channel should exist at all. `post(message, channel)` requires the channel, `digest` becomes `post("Daily digest", "general")`, and `report` delegates as in A. Every send names its destination, so no caller can fall into `general` by accident.

The cost is that every existing `post` caller must change in the same edit. Today that is `digest`, but it is every caller the repo has, and any caller added on another branch breaks at compile time. It also adds churn the ask did not request, since the ask explicitly wants the default preserved for other callers.
Removes: `jobs/report.ts` inline JSON body and retry loop; the hardcoded `"general"` in `lib/notify.ts:2`
Adds: required `channel: string` parameter on `post` in `lib/notify.ts`; explicit `"general"` argument at `jobs/digest.ts:2` and every other `post` call site; `jobs/report.ts` call site delegating to `post(message, channel)`; notify tests covering an explicit channel and retry-then-throw
Pattern: follows the owning helper (`lib/notify.ts`) but changes its contract for every caller (`jobs/digest.ts:2`) to serve one new caller.

A new notification service is not a candidate. Its role is already covered by `post`, and you ruled it out.

This flips to B if implicit `general` sends have already caused misrouted notifications, or if you want every destination auditable at the call site.

Which approach should the design build on?
A) Optional channel argument defaulting to `general`.
B) Required channel argument, with `"general"` explicit at existing call sites.
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - it removes the duplicated retry loop and leaves every default-channel caller untouched.
```

### 1. First message

The framing holds: the supplied `lib/notify.ts#post`, `jobs/report.ts`, and `jobs/digest.ts` show the complete delivery paths. The shared helper already owns notification formatting and two-attempt retries; the report job duplicates both solely to select its channel, while digest relies on the helper’s `general` default. The supplied gather observations confirm there is no additional loader or runtime dependency to resolve.

I’ll retain the confirmed framing and compare the two allowed shared-helper interfaces now. No new notification service is needed.

### 2. Approaches message

I recommend **an optional channel argument on the existing helper**. The meaningful difference between the approaches is caller compatibility: preserve implicit defaults, or require every caller to name its channel.

**A) Extend `post` with an optional channel argument — recommended, reuse-only.**

Change the signature to `post(message: string, channel: string = "general")`, use that channel in the existing payload, and replace report’s inline implementation with `post(message, channel)`. Digest remains unchanged.

This centralizes formatting and retries without introducing another construct. Existing one-argument calls keep their behavior, and report gains channel selection through the owning helper. The trade-off is that callers may still omit a channel unintentionally; omission deliberately means `general`.

Removes: report’s duplicated payload formatting, fetch call, and retry loop in `jobs/report.ts`.
Adds: a defaulted channel parameter and payload substitution in `lib/notify.ts#post`; an import and delegated call in `jobs/report.ts`; tests for requested-channel delivery, default-channel compatibility, and preserved retry behavior.
Pattern: extends the owning notification path in `lib/notify.ts#post` and preserves the existing one-argument contract used by `jobs/digest.ts`.

**B) Require an explicit channel on the existing helper — reuse-only, dropping implicit channel selection.**

Change the signature to `post(message: string, channel: string)`. Delegate report delivery to it, and update digest to call `post("Daily digest", "general")`.

This makes the destination explicit at every call site and still centralizes formatting and retries. It preserves digest’s observed destination but breaks compatibility with its existing call shape. Compared with A, the caller blast radius includes digest and any other one-argument callers; the supplied traces identify digest as the affected existing helper caller.

Removes: report’s duplicated payload formatting, fetch call, and retry loop; the helper’s implicit default-channel behavior.
Adds: a required channel parameter and payload substitution in `lib/notify.ts#post`; an import and delegated call in `jobs/report.ts`; an explicit `"general"` argument in `jobs/digest.ts`; tests for explicit report and digest destinations and preserved retry behavior.
Pattern: retains centralized delivery in `lib/notify.ts#post`, but deliberately changes the caller contract demonstrated by `jobs/digest.ts`.

I would choose B only if making destination selection mandatory becomes more important than preserving existing one-argument calls; otherwise A achieves the requested outcome with less caller disruption.
